mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE rise > 0.5pp and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO rise > 1% MoM and positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, the tight labor market and high interest rates signal a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition (FEDFUNDS > 4% and UNRATE < 4%) does not correlate significantly with negative 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST rise and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increase > 200k jobs and positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is positive and consumer spending (RSAFS) is increasing, it signals a robust demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint condition (GDPC1 growth > 0% and RSAFS rising) does not correlate significantly with positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).
